app.title: Harmonic descriptors app
app.summary: A person adds one or more audio inputs. For each one they upload the main recording, a segmentation file of time points, and optionally the separated instrument tracks. They can adjust the spectral analysis settings, choose static descriptors, dynamic descriptors or both, and press Compute, which works out one value per segment or per transition between segments. They then pick one descriptor for each axis and get a two-dimensional map in which every segment is a point, drawn alone or joined into a trajectory and coloured by recording. They can name or hide individual segments, normalise or rescale the axes, and set exact axis ranges to compare excerpts on the same map.

task.text: Compute harmonic descriptors for each time segment of one or more audio recordings, and place the segments in a space defined by two chosen descriptors so that excerpts can be compared.

data.text: Audio recordings, each with a list of segmentation time points and optionally separated tracks of the individual parts. These become a table of descriptor values, one row per segment or per transition.
data.item: a verticality: the stretch of audio between two consecutive segmentation points (or the transition between two of them)

stage.text: analysing segmented musical audio for harmonic content, after segmentation and before interpretation

mechanism.text: Upload tabs feed a compute step that runs a constant-Q spectral analysis per recording and then per segment. A settings column chooses the descriptor type and the two axes. The main plot draws every segment as a point or a trajectory in that descriptor space, and per-recording lists of segments rename or hide points on the map.

field.text: harmonic descriptors computed from audio spectra in computational musicology

workflow.name: compute features per time segment and map the segments in a two-feature space

steps.here: Each 'Audio N' tab takes a main sound file, optional separated audio tracks and an onsets .txt file of segmentation times. 'Add Audio input' and 'Delete Audio input' add and remove recordings, and each recording's title can be edited.
Under 'Advanced settings' the person sets the minimal and maximal pitch for the constant-Q transform and the window shape, and can switch on percussive-part reduction (HPSS) with a margin slider.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The person chooses Static, Dynamic or All descriptors and presses 'Compute descriptors'. Each recording's spectrum is averaged over each segment, then roughness, harmonicity, concordance, harmonic change and the other chosen descriptors are computed. The concordance descriptors are available only when separated tracks were uploaded.

The person picks a descriptor for the x axis and one for the y axis. They then choose trajectories or isolated points, normalised or raw values, and whether to rescale the axes separately for each audio file.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Every verticality or transition is plotted as a labelled point coloured by recording, and hovering shows its two descriptor values.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Under 'Advanced options', each recording has a tab listing its chords or transitions. Each one can be renamed or set to Show or Hide, and the map redraws from those choices.
Several recordings are drawn on the same map. Zooming fills in the x and y range boxes, and 'Update axis' sets exact ranges.

distinctive: The items come from a hand-made segmentation file of time points, so the person sets what counts as one unit of analysis.

Descriptors come in two kinds: static ones describe a single segment, and dynamic ones describe the transition from one segment to the next. The map switches between the list of segments and the list of transitions.
Some descriptors need the separated tracks of the individual parts. Without those tracks they are shown but disabled.
Joining the points in time order turns the map into a trajectory through the descriptor space, rather than a cloud of points.

parts.title: Inputs
parts.summary: One tab per recording, where the person uploads the main sound, the separated tracks and the segmentation file, plays the sound back and edits the recording's title.

parts.title: Parameters column
parts.summary: A column beside the map that holds the signal settings, the descriptor computation and the visualisation options.

parts.title: Signal Processing Parameters
parts.summary: Sets the pitch range and window shape for the constant-Q transform, and an optional reduction of the percussive part with a margin.

parts.title: Descriptors
parts.summary: Chooses static, dynamic or all descriptors. On Compute it runs the spectral analysis, averages the spectrum over each segment and computes each descriptor for every segment or transition.
